title: Papaya: modeled ₹416/qtl left, Solan → Kangra (Baijnath)
summary: January 2021: reported papaya prices at Solan and Kangra (Baijnath) imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 78% of 23 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹416 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 72 same-variety market pairs screened for papaya in January 2021; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) at both markets; sale matched to the first Kangra (Baijnath) report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: January 2021
scenes.caption: Solan (Himachal Pradesh) and Kangra (Baijnath) (Himachal Pradesh) both reported papaya prices for the same variety and grade (Medium) on 23 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Solan reported a median ₹2,200 per quintal. Kangra (Baijnath) reported a median ₹2,900 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹700/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹700 per quintal, and Kangra (Baijnath) was dearer on 96% of days.

scenes.headline: 251 km by road
scenes.caption: 251 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~4 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹54/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹376 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹216 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Kangra (Baijnath) report, the rule selects 19 of 22 modeled shipping days. 18 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹416 per quintal (₹257 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Papaya route from Solan to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 78% of matched days in January 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹41,600, or ₹25,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to papaya
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹54/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Papaya route from Solan to Kangra (Baijnath) was positive on 78% of matched days in January 2021. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹41,600, or ₹25,700 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.
